work.text: Between 1829 and 1833, Hokusai created a print series depicting thirty-six views of the mountain, including this one, sometimes known as “Red Fuji.”

source.author: Cleveland Museum of Art
source.title: Collection description: South Wind, Clear Sky, from Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji

moment.text: Mt. Fuji, Japan’s highest mountain, appeared in most Japanese 19th-century travel literature. Maps sometimes showed its location with a Fuji-shaped icon and indicated where travelers could get the best view of it.

source.author: Cleveland Museum of Art

matters.text: The season in this scene is a time between late summer and early autumn, when the mountain takes on a reddish hue.
